source.ref: kubernetes-sigs/aws-load-balancer-controller @ v3.6.2 (clone HEAD 745586f6a, 2026-10-28) read on the release branches origin/release-2.4 … origin/release-3.6 plus the GitHub release bodies v2.4.0 … v3.6.2
source.note: The AWS Load Balancer Controller publishes NO per-version Kubernetes compatibility matrix — supportWindows is deliberately NULL. docs/deploy/installation.md 'Supported Kubernetes versions' states only a FLOOR per line ('v2.4.0+ requires Kubernetes 1.19+', 'v2.5.0+ requires Kubernetes 1.22+', unchanged through v3.6.2) and every GitHub release title repeats it ('v3.6.2 (requires Kubernetes 1.22+)'); a floor with no ceiling is not a window, so it is carried as the 2.4 / 2.5 floor rules in k8s-rules/aws-load-balancer-controller and never transcribed into a row. NEVER derive a window from go.mod (k8s.io/api v0.36.x at v3.6.2 says nothing about what the controller was tested against). The forced hop is therefore CURRENCY only: latestKnownVersion is 3.6.2 (the newest release tag, a PATCH so that introducedIn-pinned rules — 3.4.3 rule-per-hostname, 3.6.2 base-image CAs — are selected correctly) and this hop is NOT a Kubernetes-compatibility claim; every surface that renders it must say so (AddonCompatAnalyzer.HopReason.CURRENCY). What docs/index.md DOES publish (section 'Support Policy', since 1abc9bb0f 2023-10-13, unchanged at v3.6.2) is a support POLICY — 'Currently, AWS provides security updates and bug fixes to the latest available minor versions of AWS LBC. For other ad-hoc supports on older versions, please reach out through AWS support ticket.' — transcribed as supportedMinorsBehindLatest=0: an installed minor below latestKnownVersion's (3.6) gets the MEDIUM outside-vendor-support finding, across the 2.x → 3.x major too. No end-of-life DATES are published (and endoflife.date has no entry), so no VENDOR_EOL hop exists and the Maintain lifecycle feed carries nothing for it. rules and upgradeNotes are EMPTY BY DESIGN: the breaking changes live in the generated-rule pipeline (kb/aws-load-balancer-controller -> k8s-rules/aws-load-balancer-controller), extracted mechanically from FOUR upstream paths because the repository has no CHANGELOG file and only a v1->v2 migration guide: (A) the GitHub release bodies' 'Action required' / 'Upgrade Notes' sections (committed snapshot under kb/aws-load-balancer-controller/upstream/), (B) the docs diffed between adjacent RELEASE BRANCHES (docs/deploy, docs/guide/{ingress,service,targetgroupbinding,gateway}), (C) code ledgers diffed per release branch (IAM policy actions, flag defaults, feature-gate defaults, CRD served/storage versions, admission webhooks and their failurePolicy, chart values) and (D) the sigs.k8s.io/gateway-api dependency pin. Detection: the controller image repository ends in eks/aws-load-balancer-controller (public.ecr.aws/eks/aws-load-balancer-controller and the ECR mirrors 602401143452.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/amazon/aws-load-balancer-controller are both served through the public ECR path on EKS add-on and Helm installs); the v1 docker.io/amazon/aws-alb-ingress-controller image does NOT match and is a different, retired product. The controller's own CRs (TargetGroupBinding, IngressClassParams, ALBTargetControlConfig, the gateway.k8s.aws configurations) are collected by the agent arm (slice S2, agent 0.4.154+, org toggle aws-load-balancer-controller, keys/presence/enums/names only — the fingerprint's collection block names the kinds); inventoryKinds stays EMPTY because the generated rules read those rows through the evaluator, not through the legacy per-kind CR fetch this field drives.
